The investment of writing path-addressed documentation once amortises across every operator who opens the artifact, and survives future bank-format changes because the path pattern is durable while NODE_IDs are tree-extraction-specific.

rules.rule: When documenting a SAP migration project in the companion HTML (or any operator-facing artifact), split content into two clearly-distinct zones: (1) Current Solution / V000 baseline — how the system is wired and behaving today, organized per object (per tree, per program, per workflow), and (2) Change Strategy / V001 changes — the specific deltas the project introduces, also organized per object. Cross-reference between the two zones with explicit links so a reader looking at a V001 delta can jump to the V000 baseline for that same object, and vice versa. Do NOT mix V000 baseline content with V001 delta content in the same section — the cognitive cost of switching context line-by-line is high, and operators reading for one specific object end up scrolling through unrelated other-object material.
rules.why: Session #65 user pushback on the DMEE Configuration tab: 'maybe some information should be moved to Current Solution and only keep the specific changes here'. Root cause: the original tab mixed V000 baseline material (tree structure ASCII, 6-tabs settings, hierarchy stratification, screenshots of the today-state) with V001 delta material (per-target INSERTs, Step A/B/C walkthroughs, code-change indicators). Operators reading for ONE tree had to scroll through both kinds of content for SEPA (used as worked example) before reaching their tree's specific deltas. The cleaner split: V000 baseline content lives in Current Solution per-tree; V001 delta content lives in Change Strategy → DMEE Configuration per-tree sub-tabs. Each tree's V001 sub-tab carries a back-link to its V000 baseline; each V000 baseline carries a forward-link to its V001 deltas. Result: operators reading one tree end-to-end open just two locations (V000 + V001) instead of scrolling through all-tree concept material first.
rules.how_to_apply: When creating or restructuring a companion that documents a SAP migration project: 1. Identify the units of work (trees, programs, workflows, configurations). 2. Allocate two zones: Current Solution (V000 baseline per unit) + Change Strategy (V001 deltas per unit). 3. For each unit, write a self-contained section in BOTH zones: V000 section describes how it works today;    V001 section describes the specific changes. 4. Add explicit cross-references at the top of each section pointing to its counterpart in the other zone. 5. Cross-tree concepts (rules that apply to all units — e.g. 'UI indentation = XML nesting depth') live in    the V001 zone foundations sub-tab OR in a shared concept page; not duplicated per unit. 6. When a V001 change explicitly references a V000 element (e.g. 'INSERT child under existing PstlAdr'),    the V001 prose says 'see Current Solution → Tree X for the V000 baseline of PstlAdr'. 7. Sub-tabs in the sidebar (one per unit) make navigation explicit — the operator clicks the unit they care    about and reads end-to-end. APPLIES TO: companion HTML pages, multi-page knowledge artifacts, project plans. DOES NOT APPLY TO: brain JSON, raw matrix CSVs, or any non-stakeholder-facing artifact.
rules.source_file: Session #65 BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html restructure (DMEE Configuration tab split into foundations + 4 per-tree sub-tabs; Current Solution gained per-tree V000 baseline section)
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-001 'Knowledge over velocity': mixing V000 baseline with V001 changes is faster to write because there's no second zone to maintain, but operators pay the cognitive cost on every read. Splitting once (zones + cross-references) amortises across every operator who reads the companion thereafter. Also CP-002 (preserve first): the V000 baseline IS knowledge that must survive even after V001 cutover — having it in its own zone protects it from being conflated with deltas.

rules.statement: When triaging UNESCO field-office support tickets reporting 'insufficient budget' or 'red notification' on SES/MIRO/F110 for donor (Type 101-112) funds, ALWAYS check whether the fund's project title contains an explicit biennium tag like '(2024-2025)' or '(2026-2027)'. If so, check whether a successor biennium fund exists by searching funds for FINCODE one digit higher (e.g. 196EAR4042 -> 196EAR4043) AND whether the successor's PROJ.POST1 explicitly names the new biennium. If both conditions hold, the predecessor fund is a biennium-end starvation candidate and the immediate workaround is FMAVCREINIT on (RLDNR=9H, predecessor fund, current RYEAR).
rules.why: INC-000005638 (2026-05-01): Without this rule, the analyst would burn cycles checking ZXFMYU22 10-digit hard link, ZXFMDTU02 hardcodes, ZXFMCU17 tolerance cap, and ZXM06U22 release strategy - all of which pass clean. The actual root cause is at the AVC pool / biennium-close-out process layer, not in custom code. UNESCO's biennium pattern is highly regular (196EAR4037 through 4043 covering 2014-2015 through 2026-2027 in 2-year increments) and reading PROJ.POST1 reveals it in seconds. The detector inc5638_avc_fipex_deficit.py confirms 2,153 of 2,708 (79.5pct) donor (FUND, FUNDSCTR) buckets fit this class signature - this is not a per-incident defect, it is a recurring class.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. Confirm the user's reported PO/SES touches a fund. 2. Read funds.TYPE (must be 101-112 for donor scope). 3. Read proj.POST1 - look for biennium tag like '(YYYY-YYYY)'. 4. If biennium found, check whether successor fund exists: SELECT * FROM funds WHERE FINCODE = predecessor_FINCODE_with_last_digit_incremented. 5. If successor exists AND its proj.POST1 names the new biennium, you are likely in INC-000005638 class. 6. Confirm via Zagentexecution/quality_checks/inc5638_avc_fipex_deficit.py. 7. Recommend FMAVCREINIT and biennium-close-out review. 8. DO NOT spend cycles on ZXFMYU22 hardcodes / FMDERIVE / tolerance caps unless the predecessor fund is NOT a biennium type.

rules.rule: When an availability/budget incident is reported (TCODE in {ML81N, F110, F-53, MIRO, FB60, FBV0, FMBB, FMX1}, error class FMAVC*, BP6*, ZFI*, RW609 with a budget keyword), pull BOTH the FM-AVC pool AND the PS-AVC pool BEFORE declaring a root cause. Never conclude the firing engine on the basis of message vocabulary or domain-prefix alone.
rules.why: INC-000005638 first pass concluded FM-side root cause and built a class detector with 79.5% hit rate -- which the user correctly flagged as 'too broad'. Pulling BPJA/COSP/FMAVCT showed the actual firing engine is FM-AVC at the AVC-DERIVED bucket level, not at any FIPEX or fund level. Without the PS data we could not even rule out PS-AVC, and without FMAVCT proper (vs the useless fmavct_summary) we could not see the TC bucket starvation. The fund-level FM pool was +$11.83M while the actual TC bucket was -$1.56M -- the difference between 'looks healthy' and 'every SES blocks'.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Resolve the WBS (PS_PSP_PNR) for every PO line via EKKN.
2. Compute PS-AVC pool at the project level (sum BPJA WRTTP=41 minus COSP WRTTP=04+22 across the biennium).
3. Compute FM-AVC pool at the AVC-DERIVED bucket: revenue (FMIFIIT WRTTP=66 with FIPEX in the FMAFMAP013500109 derivation range for that fund) MINUS consumption (FMAVCT KBFC for the matching bucket).
4. Tag the firing engine: BOTH if both pools < 0, FM if only FM, PS if only PS. Cite TIER_1 evidence: file:line for code, rfc_pull for data.
5. Only after the engine is identified, recommend a fix path.

rules.rule: If revenue (WRTTP=66) is loaded on a placeholder FIPEX (commonly 'REVENUE') while consumption lands on operational FIPEX values, AND the AVC derivation rule (FMAFMAP013500109 step 0007) does NOT include the placeholder FIPEX in the same range as the operational ones, the AVC bucket sees zero revenue and full consumption — pool goes negative even though the fund-level pool is healthy. This is a SYSTEMIC pattern across UNESCO Type 101-112 funds (1,330 buckets in Tier 2 of the misalignment classifier as of 2026-05-01). It is NOT biennium-specific.
rules.why: INC-000005638 is the first concrete instance proven with TIER_1 RFC data. Without recognising this pattern, the agent will (a) chase per-fund or per-FIPEX deficits as the root cause, (b) recommend FMAVCREINIT or biennium close-out which do NOT fix the underlying mismatch, (c) miss the systemic scale of the issue (1,787 buckets affected across UNESCO).
rules.how_to_apply:
When examining an FM-AVC pool deficit:
1. Pull FMAFMAP013500109 entries for the fund and identify the AVC-derived range.
2. Check whether revenue (WRTTP=66) FIPEX values ARE INCLUDED in any rule range. If they are loaded on a FIPEX that is NOT in any range (e.g. 'REVENUE'), the misalignment exists.
3. Recommend either (a) extend the AVC derivation rule to include the revenue FIPEX, OR (b) refactor the revenue-posting integration (often MuleSoft for UNESCO) to apportion across operational FIPEX. Both fix the class at once.

rules.rule: When pulling FMAVCT, ALWAYS include RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM and ALLOCTYPE_9 in the field list -- they are non-key tracking columns but they are the ONLY way to identify which (Fund x FundCenter x AVC-bucket) the row belongs to. The primary key COBJNR is an opaque 36-char internal hash. RCMMTITEM holds the AVC-DERIVED bucket (PC/TC/NPC or literal FIPEX), NOT the original FIPEX from the posting.
rules.why: First INC-005638 extraction pulled (RLDNR, RFIKRS, COBJNR, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, RTCUR, HSL01, HSLVT) — 8 fields, the safe ceiling. Result: every row had identical opaque COBJNR and the data was useless for AVC bucket analysis. Re-pulling with (RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, HSL01) revealed the actual TC vs 80 vs literal-FIPEX bucket structure.
rules.how_to_apply: Slim 7-field set: RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM, RYEAR, ALLOCTYPE_9, HSL01. If you need additional periods, do a second pull with HSL02-HSL16 keyed on the same row identifiers.

rules.rule: UNESCO's FMAVCT only stores ALLOCTYPE_9='KBFC' (consumption) rows -- never KBFB (budget). The pool depth at any AVC bucket must be computed JOINING FMIFIIT (revenue side, WRTTP=66) and FMAVCT (consumption side, KBFC). Querying FMAVCT alone for 'budget vs consumption' is WRONG.
rules.why: Default mental model is FMAVCT has both budget and consumption rows. UNESCO's config does not. Several FM-AVC analyses across sessions inferred 'fund is depleted' from FMAVCT alone -- they were measuring consumption only, not pool depth.
rules.how_to_apply: Pool depth = sum(FMIFIIT FKBTR WHERE FONDS=F AND FISTL=FC AND WRTTP=66 AND GJAHR=Y AND FIPEX in derivation_range_for_bucket(B)) MINUS sum(FMAVCT HSL01 WHERE RFUND=F AND RFUNDSCTR=FC AND RCMMTITEM=B AND RYEAR=Y AND ALLOCTYPE_9='KBFC').

rules.rule: RFC_READ_TABLE on EKKN has a hard 8-field ceiling. Pulling 9+ fields raises AD/E/718 (TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA / buffer overflow) even on tiny WHERE clauses. Same applies to BPJA, BPDJ, COSP, COSS — all wide tables.
rules.why: Discovered 2026-05-01 during INC-005638 extension. Initial extraction with 25 fields failed cryptically; the splitter fallback worked but required recursion. The cleanest path is to plan a slim 7-8 field set up front based on what the analysis actually needs.
rules.how_to_apply:
When designing a new RFC extraction for any table with > 50 fields:
1. Write down the 5-7 columns the analysis truly needs.
2. Add 1-2 join-key columns to enable downstream JOINs.
3. Verify total row width < ~250 bytes (each char field ~16-24 bytes, each CURR/QUAN ~16 bytes).
4. If you need more, plan a second pull keyed on the same row identifiers. Do NOT rely on the recursive splitter -- it loses the row-alignment guarantee on heterogeneous WHEREs.

rules.rule: Before describing SAP mechanism behavior in companions, specs, or operator playbooks, validate against SAP Help Portal + screenshots of the actual customer system. Brain claims, intuition, or session-derived models can be wrong on mechanisms that have not been exercised in production yet.
rules.why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the companion's V001 deployment strategy was built on an 'atomic flag flip via EX_STATUS' model with 'rollback in seconds'. Deep research against SAP Help Portal (Version Management, Activating Format Trees, function module DMEE_GET_BACK_ACTIVE_TREE_ABA, R3TR DMEE workbench class confirmation) + 5 tx DMEE screenshots from UNESCO P01 revealed the real SAP-standard behavior is fundamentally different: V001 activation OVERWRITES V000 (content replacement, not flag flip); rollback requires a Generate Version snapshot taken BEFORE activation (not pre-positioned transport); transport class is Workbench (R3TR DMEE), not Customizing. Brain claim 102 said 'first-ever V001 transport at UNESCO' which was true but the team had built deployment mechanics on assumptions about how that transport would behave at activation — assumptions that did not match SAP standard. The wrong model would have caused: (a) V000 unrecoverable after Phase 5 cutover (no snapshot prep step), (b) failed rollback procedure under pressure, (c) misclassified transport-class approval chain (W vs K reviewer requirements differ). Caught this session because user pushed back on the magic-feeling explanation and demanded SAP-official sources.
rules.how_to_apply:
When writing about SAP mechanism behavior (DMEE versioning, BAdI dispatch, transport semantics, F110 internals, BCM workflow logic, etc.) in any operator-facing artifact:
1. Identify each load-bearing mechanism claim ('atomic flip', 'rollback in seconds', 'snapshot preserved', 'transport class W', etc.).
2. For each claim, find SAP-Help-Portal-level evidence OR a screenshot from the actual customer system OR SAP-shipped function module documentation. Brain TIER_1 claims about UNESCO state are NOT sufficient evidence for SAP mechanism behavior — those are about UNESCO, not about SAP standard.
3. If evidence is missing, mark the claim '[INFERRED]' or '[VERIFICATION PENDING]'. Do not present unverified mechanism claims as operational instructions.
4. For Phase 5-style cutover plans specifically: validate the cutover and rollback procedure end-to-end against SAP-official docs before publishing to operators. Mistakes on cutover mechanics are high-impact (production payment files, bank acceptance, audit trail).
5. When pushing back from a user surfaces a 'this looks like magic' / 'I do not see this in the UI' moment: take it seriously, do the deep research, do not defend the existing model.
6. After a correction is applied, delete the contradicting content (do not leave it as 'historical') — the SAP-CORRECTION callout itself is the historical record.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-003 (Precision, evidence, facts) — the rule is a direct application: every operational claim must be anchored in maximum precision + verifiable evidence + checkable facts. Brain claims are necessary but not sufficient when the claim is about SAP mechanism behavior; SAP-Help-Portal-level sources or live system screenshots are required. The session #66 correction (DMEE versioning model) was the second-order CP-003 violation: the brain had TIER_1 facts about UNESCO state (claim 109 V001 byte-equal V000) but the deployment strategy was layered on top with TIER_3 inferred mechanism behavior treated as TIER_1. The fix forces the verification gate at the boundary between project facts and SAP mechanism claims.

violations_observed.evidence: Companion described V001 cutover as 'atomic flag flip on EX_STATUS, rollback in seconds via flip back, V000 preserved automatically' — all three claims contradicted by SAP Help Portal which says activation overwrites V000 with V001 content; rollback requires Version Management retrieve of a pre-saved snapshot; preservation requires manual Generate Version before activation. 380 lines of lifecycle/playbook content had to be deleted and replaced after deep research.

rules.rule: Before settling on a Phase-3-style testing methodology for a SAP runtime change, systematically walk the tx-level Test/Simulate menu options of the affected module. SAP runtime engines (DMEE, SAPFPAYM, BAdI test harnesses, etc.) typically expose their runtime input structures directly in a built-in test mode. These test modes accept manual or copy-pasted data and run the engine against it without upstream stages — enabling history-replay testing without F110 (or equivalent upstream caller).
rules.why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the project had a Python simulator (claim 105) for fast schema validation and a planned 'Activate V001 in D01 + F110' for full-stack validation. The middle ground — tx DMEE → Tree → Test with hand-crafted FPAYHX/FPAYH/FPAYP — was overlooked entirely until the user spotted the screen layout and pointed out that 'the columns ARE the runtime buffers, F110 just fills them automatically'. This unlocked layer 3 of the testing methodology: SAP-engine-accurate validation against historical production patterns (REGUH/REGUP reconstruction → paste → run) without requiring F110 in any system. Without this layer, Phase 3 testing was scheduled to depend on D01 F110 batch runs which are 30 min each and require the V001 activation transport. With layer 3, the top-15 scenarios (94.5% volume coverage) can be validated in ~30 min TOTAL using REGUH/REGUP reconstruction + paste-and-run in tx DMEE Test Data. As a derivative benefit, the test screen reveals which V001 MP_SC_FLD bindings are SAP-standard (visible) vs UNESCO-custom append (hidden in CI_FPAYHX) — a portability audit by inspection.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. When designing a Phase-3 test strategy for any SAP runtime change, list the tx-codes that drive the runtime chain.
2. For each tx-code, walk the menu items: look for Test, Simulate, Trial, 'Display Test Data', or similar — they are usually under Tree/Tools/Utilities/Goto menus.
3. If a Test mode exposes input structures: those structures are the runtime entry point — testing can start there, skipping upstream stages.
4. Document the test mode in the testing-methodology section of the spec/companion alongside any pure-software simulator and any full-stack integration test.
5. Stratify test cases across the available layers (typical 4 layers): (a) fast/cheap simulator for design iteration; (b) SAP-native test mode hand-crafted for engine-accuracy spot-checks; (c) SAP-native test mode + database-reconstructed history for production-pattern coverage; (d) full-stack with real upstream invocation for final integration.
6. Critically: examine which fields are visible in the test mode by default — they are the SAP-standard runtime structure. Fields hidden in 'More Fields' or append-structure layouts are customer extensions; bindings to those are non-portable to other systems.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-001 (Knowledge over velocity) — this is a discovery-discipline rule. The DMEE Test Data feature was always present in tx DMEE but never inspected during Phase 0-1 testing-methodology design. Velocity prioritised 'we have a Python simulator + D01 F110, that's enough' over the slower act of walking the SAP transaction menus to find what else was already available. The cost of that velocity was an avoidable gap in the testing layers (no SAP-engine-accurate middle layer between simulator and full F110). The rule forces a discovery pass before testing-methodology lock-in.

violations_observed.evidence: Phase 0/1 testing methodology was designed with 2 layers (Python simulator + D01 F110) and the project shipped to Phase 2 build with that plan. The 3rd layer (tx DMEE → Tree → Test with FPAYHX/FPAYH/FPAYP buffer-paste) was discovered Session #66 only because the user took a screenshot of the DMEE Test Data screen and recognised the input structures as the runtime buffers F110 fills. Had this discovery happened in Phase 0, the testing matrix would have been planned differently and Phase 3 effort estimate would have been ~30 min for top-15 scenarios instead of N hours of D01 F110 batch coordination.

rules.title: When user reports budget exceeded on UNESCO funds, ALWAYS test BOTH FM-AVC bucket and PS-AVC pool BEFORE attributing to one engine
rules.why: INC-000005638 demonstrated that 'insuffisance de budget' from a UNESCO user is ambiguous: PS-AVC project pool can be +$16M while FM-AVC TC bucket is in -$1.5M deficit on the SAME (Fund, FundCenter) tuple. Inferring engine from user terminology is unsafe.
rules.how_to_apply: Before attributing a 'budget exceeded' incident to PS-AVC OR FM-AVC, compute both pools: (a) PS-AVC = sum bpja_*.WTJHR WRTTP=41 over the project's WBS minus sum cosp_*.WTG001..WTG003 WRTTP IN ('04','22'); (b) FM-AVC bucket = sum fmifiit_full.FKBTR WRTTP=66 in AVC-derivation FIPEX range minus sum fmavct_*.HSL01 ALLOCTYPE_9=KBFC at the (RFIKRS, RFUND, RFUNDSCTR, RCMMTITEM) bucket. Run inc5638_per_po_engine_analysis.py-style logic and report verdict={FM | PS | BOTH | NEITHER}.
rules.anti_pattern: Defaulting to PS-AVC because the user said 'budget exceeded on a project' without testing FM-AVC at the AVC-derived bucket level.

rules.title: When triaging an AVC budget block, ALWAYS check the class detector first to determine if it is one-off or class-of-defect
rules.rule: When a user reports an FMAVC005 / FI 026 / 'insuffisance de budget' on a TYPE 101-112 donor fund, the FIRST action is to run the class detector inc5638_fm_ps_avc_misalignment.py against the latest Gold DB and check whether the affected (Fund, FundCenter) bucket is part of the 2,005-bucket MODEL-GAP-2026-001 class. If yes: stop investigating as a one-off, escalate as class instance. If no: proceed with per-incident analysis but capture the result in the recurring detector for future class-membership re-evaluation.
rules.why: Session #66/67 (INC-000005638) demonstrated that an apparent 'one-off' fund-level budget block was the canonical case of a 2,005-bucket structural class growing +4.1%/month. Without class-membership awareness, incident analysts are doomed to repeatedly re-discover the same root cause from scratch on every new ticket against a TYPE 101-112 donor fund. The detector+CSV pre-computes class membership; not consulting it is a velocity loss AND an evidence loss (one-off framing leaves the class footprint hidden from management). CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) and CP-003 (evidence-anchored).
rules.how_to_apply:
1. On ticket arrival, parse the FONDS / FUNDSCTR / CommItem (or AVC-bucket) from the user's screenshot/SU53.
2. Open Zagentexecution/quality_checks/inc5638_fm_ps_avc_misalignment.csv (latest run) and grep the (FUND, FUNDSCTR, BUCKET) tuple.
3. If the tuple appears with Tier in {1, 2}: this is an instance of MODEL-GAP-2026-001. Annotate the incident accordingly, link to canonical doc knowledge/incidents/INC-000005638_ses_block_donor_fund_avc_fipex_deficit.md, propose the standard remediation (FMAVCREINIT / FMBB / TYPE 104->106 close). Do NOT redo full root-cause analysis from scratch.
4. If the tuple does NOT appear (or appears with Tier in {3, 4}): proceed with per-incident analysis but log the result back into the detector so the next class-detector run captures it. Open a known_unknown if the bucket pattern is novel.
5. Re-run the class detector at most weekly so CSV stays current. Log the run timestamp + Tier 1/2 counts in brain_state.data_quality and check growth rate vs 2026-05-01 baseline (+4.1%/month).
rules.anti_pattern: Re-running per-PO engine analysis from scratch on every new FMAVC005 ticket without first checking class-detector membership. Reporting an incident as 'one-off' when the (Fund, FundCenter, Bucket) is in the 2,005-bucket class.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) — the rule preserves class-of-defect knowledge across incident tickets so each new instance is a 30-second class-lookup, not a 30-minute re-discovery. Also touches CP-003 (precision/evidence) because class-membership lookup is anchored in a TIER_1 CSV, not analyst judgment.

rules.rule: tx DMEE 'Format tree → Test active version' (F8) tests ONLY the version with EX_STATUS='A'. There is NO 'Test maintenance version' option in the standard menu. To test the Maintenance version (V001) with the SAP engine, V001 MUST be activated first — which (per SAP-correct lifecycle) overwrites V000 with V001 content. Therefore V001 engine-level testing requires activation, and activation requires a Generate Version snapshot of the prior V000 BEFORE activation as the rollback enabler. V001 testing is therefore a D01-only activity (never P01) with strict snapshot+activate+test+rollback discipline.
rules.why: Session #66 (2026-05-01): the user surfaced a screenshot of the tx DMEE Format tree menu. The only test option visible was 'Test active version (F8)'. Earlier guidance assumed V001 (Maintenance) could be tested in isolation by 'switching to Maintenance version and clicking Test' — that is not how the standard menu works. SAP's design assumption is: production-grade testing of a tree happens AFTER activation, on the active state. The maintenance version is for editing, not for production-grade test runs. This constrains the 4-layer testing methodology: Layer 2-3 (DMEE Test Data) tests V000 only without activation; testing V001 with the SAP engine requires Layer 4 (D01 activation with snapshot+rollback). The Python simulator (Layer 1) is therefore essential for V001 design iteration, with engine equivalence proven on V000 transitively.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. When designing a DMEE test methodology, distinguish two separate engine-level test paths: (a) V000 testing — works directly in any system via F8 'Test active version' on the production state, no activation needed; (b) V001 testing — requires activation in a non-production system (D01) with the SAP-correct 4-step ritual: snapshot V000 to historical version (Generate Version → V002), activate V001 (overwrites V000), test the new V000 (= V001 content), retrieve V002 to restore original V000.
2. NEVER attempt V001 engine testing in P01. The activation overwrite is the same in any system; only D01 has the rollback latitude (V01 is shared UAT, P01 is production).
3. Maintain the Python simulator (or equivalent) as Layer 1 for V001 design iteration without engine testing. The simulator's V001 prediction is trusted by transitive equivalence once L1 V000 ≡ L2 (engine) V000 is empirically confirmed for the same scenarios.
4. In test runbooks, label phases explicitly: 'Phase A — Test V000 (any system, no activation)' vs 'Phase B — Test V001 (D01 only, activation+rollback ritual mandatory)'. Do not let operators conflate the two.
5. When documenting V001 test procedure, always include the snapshot pre-step and the rollback post-step — they are not optional.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-003 (Precision, evidence, facts) — the rule corrects an imprecise earlier claim. Initial guidance said 'switch to Maintenance version and run Test' as if both V000 and V001 testing were symmetric in tx DMEE. The screenshot from the user proved otherwise — SAP exposes only 'Test active version' (F8). The earlier framing was inferred from SAP help docs without checking the actual menu. The rule forces verification of the test-mode UI against the actual customer system before publishing operator-facing procedures, and explicitly distinguishes engine-level V000 testing (free) from engine-level V001 testing (requires activation+rollback discipline).

violations_observed.evidence: Excel runbook (sepa_ct_unes_test_cases.xlsx, first version) instructed operators to test V001 by 'switching to Maintenance version and clicking Test/Run' — that path does not work in the standard tx DMEE menu. User pushed back with the menu screenshot showing 'Test active version' is the only option. Runbook re-issued with explicit 17-step procedure for each case: 9 steps for V000 (Phase A) + 6 steps for V001 activate/test/rollback in D01 (Phase B) + 2 steps for diff.

rules.rule: When analyzing UNESCO SAP architecture defects, the agent role is EVALUATIVE not PRESCRIPTIVE. Do not propose code modifications, BAdI implementations, or architectural changes as if the agent were going to execute them. Document findings as OPTIONS for UNESCO config teams to evaluate.
rules.why: User directive Session #69 (2026-05-02): "No debes tocar ningún código, solo evaluar". The agent does not own or modify production SAP code. Code changes belong to UNESCO config teams (FM/PS Configuration Team, MuleSoft Ops, Architecture Board). The agent provides empirical evidence, risk classification, and structured options — UNESCO decides and executes.
rules.how_to_apply: Reframe all "FIX-X" entries from "we propose to modify" to "option UNESCO can evaluate". Use language like "if UNESCO decides to modify X, the empirical effect would be Y" rather than "we propose modifying X". Companions and briefs should be evaluative reports, not implementation plans. Keep the analytical depth; remove any executive verbs that imply agent will execute changes.

rules.rule: When designing DMEE V001 changes for production deployment, the ONLY definitive validation is an empirical XML output test from F110 + SAPFPAYM in a real environment (D01 dev minimum). RFC table extracts (REGUH/ADRC), brain claims about buffer populating mechanisms, and pattern-mirror reasoning across DMEE trees are NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. The runtime context binding (which field maps to which XML scope) cannot be predicted from static analysis alone.
rules.why: Session 2026-05-07: V001 SEPA Dbtr design used FPAYH-ZSTRA for <StrtNm> source mirroring ICTP pattern. RFC extracts (REGUH-ZSTRA + ADRC UNESCO HQ) gave false confidence — REGUH had vendor data, ADRC had paying co data, and we assumed Z-include populated FPAYH-ZSTRA contextually based on Dbtr/Cdtr scope. WRONG. F110 runtime populates FPAYH-ZSTRA with vendor address regardless of XML scope. Empirical XML output (file UNES_SOGE_03SEP.in collector 10002B 2026-05-07) showed <StrtNm>BFM/FAS/PAY</StrtNm> (vendor street) instead of expected <StrtNm>Place de Fontenoy</StrtNm> (UNESCO HQ). Same test also revealed CM005 GENERIC does NOT fire automatically without OBPM3 registration — BldgNb + PstCd rendered empty. Without empirical XML test these 2 design flaws would have transported to V01/P01 and broken SEPA payments at bank schema validation level.
rules.how_to_apply: Before any V001 transport release: 1) F110 + SAPFPAYM_MERGE end-to-end test in D01 (or dev system) — post a small payment, generate medium via SAPFPAYM_MERGE collector path, retrieve XML output from network share or FDTA. 2) Verify each PstlAdr leaf in XML matches expected for both Dbtr (paying co) AND Cdtr (vendor). 3) If D01 has BCM cross-payment-run setup blocking direct medium creation: SAPFPAYM_MERGE bypasses the gate, output goes to file system path per OBPM4 variant (UNESCO: \\hq-sapitf\SWIFT$\D01\INPUT\). 4) Skip-empirical paths (REGUH analysis only, brain claims only, pattern-mirror reasoning) are valid for hypothesis but NEVER for design closure. 5) The empirical test cost is ~30 min D01 work; the cost of skipping is potential broken production payments at bank rejection level.

rules.rule: Before describing how to do a SAP customizing action (e.g. wire a customer FM to a DMEE event, register a payment format, create a country variant), search the existing knowledge corpus for the canonical SAP-std transaction or IMG path FIRST. Do not invent SM30 / SE16 / direct table maintenance suggestions. If the user pushes back with 'this doesn't exist as a table', do NOT defend the suggestion — accept the correction and find the standard tx.
rules.why: Session #70 (2026-05-07): I told user `tx SM30 → V_T042FB → INSERT row` to register CM005 for SEPA Event 05. User correctly pushed back: 'esto no existe como tabla. No deberiamos reinventar la rueda esto es mas que comun'. The right answer was tx OBPM3 (Customer Enhancement / Function modules per format) — documented in our own repo at knowledge/domains/Payment/dme_creation_payment.md §2.3 line 72-73 since previous sessions. SAP has had OBPM3 since ECC 6.0; treating Payment Medium Workbench customizing as something requiring SM30 reinvention is a beginner-level error and propagates through to companion artifacts and execution runbooks.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. For ANY SAP customizing action (DMEE FM register, format/variant create, BAdI wiring, payment method setup), ALWAYS first grep `knowledge/domains/Payment/` and similar domain folders for the canonical TX name. dme_creation_payment.md has the full OBPM1/OBPM2/OBPM3/OBPM4 quartet with screenshots and IMG paths.
2. If knowledge corpus doesn't have it, the SAP-std customizing TX usually starts with O*: OB*, OF*, OT*, OK* — check SE93 or SAP help.
3. If TX is unknown, propose the IMG path (SPRO →) NOT the table maintenance (SM30/SE16). IMG path is human-friendly; SM30 implies you're bypassing standard customizing controls (transport recording, validation, etc).
4. NEVER suggest direct table maintenance via SM30/SE16N for tables that have a customizing wrapper TX. Direct table maintenance bypasses transport, validation, and audit trail.
5. Companion docs and runbooks must use the SAP-std TX, not invented paths. If you wrote one wrong, fix it immediately AND fix the matrix CSV / brain claims that reference it. Don't leave inconsistent documentation.

rules.rule: When dictating DMEE / SAP config values to a user mid-execution, ALWAYS validate against the EXTRACTED RFC tables (dmee_tree_node_p01.csv, dmee_tree_cond_p01.csv, etc.) BEFORE consulting derived artifacts (matrix CSVs, companion HTML tables). The matrix is a derived design artifact and may contain stale/wrong values; the RFC extraction reflects actual system state.
rules.why: Session #70 (2026-05-07): I dictated SEPA V001 leaf values to Pablo from v001_change_matrix.csv four times in succession; each time the matrix had different errors that I propagated: (1) FPAYP for SEPA Dbtr (should be FPAYHX — Dbtr is per-header, CM005 line 93 writes to FPAYHX); (2) FPAYHX for SEPA Cdtr (should be FPAYP — Cdtr is per-line, CM005 line 109 writes to FPAYP); (3) BldgNb offset 60 length 20 (should be offset 100 length 10 — CGI N_8824498030 production proves HOUSE_NUM slot is the right semantic for vendor BldgNb, not BUILDING which is empty); (4) TwnNm Dbtr REF02 (should be REF06 — REF02 is Cdtr legacy header buffer per CM005 line 130). User had to push back FOUR times — "how can it be that all fields have the same reference field?" — before I read the actual extracted CSV and corrected. Once I read dmee_tree_node_p01.csv (which I had on disk all along), all 4 errors became obvious from a single grep. The matrix had been written ~3 sessions before the final RFC extraction landed and was never reconciled.
rules.how_to_apply:
Before ANY dictation of DMEE leaf values:
1. Identify the closest 'twin' parent NODE_ID in P01 production (e.g., for SEPA Cdtr V001, use CGI N_8824498030 — same Cdtr architecture, same per-line scope, mature production pattern).
2. Read dmee_tree_node_p01.csv directly: `awk -F',' 'NR==1 || ($18 == "<parent_node>")' dmee_tree_node_p01.csv`. Show the user the EXACT extracted rows (not a paraphrase).
3. If the matrix CSV says different, treat the extracted RFC as TIER_1 ground truth. Flag the matrix discrepancy as a separate finding to update later.
4. NEVER pass values from matrix CSV to user without cross-checking against extracted CSV first. Even one cell wrong forces user to re-do the work in DMEE Tx — high-cost reversal.
5. After every batch of changes the user makes in DMEE, re-extract D01 V001 via `extract_dmee_d01_sepa_v001.py` and validate the BROTHER_ID chain + LENGTH + MP_SC_TAB/FLD/OFFSET against the master table. RFC verification is 5 seconds and catches errors that screenshots miss (cut+paste data loss, length=0 with empty source, wrong order, etc.).

rules.rule: Before proposing ANY Z-FM, BAdI extension, or custom ABAP for a DMEE leaf binding (StrtNm, BldgNb, PstCd, TwnNm, AdrLine, Ctry, etc.), parse the SAP-standard format-tree XML that ships with the relevant SAP Note for that format and enumerate every available source field — both SAP-standard (FPAYHX-AUSTO/AUST1/AUST2/AUST3, FPAYHX-LDISO, FPAYHX-ORT1Z) and customer Z-extensions on FPAYHX (e.g. UNESCO ZPFST/ZPLOR/ZLISO). Then run DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET on FPAYHX in the target system to confirm field existence + length + domain. Only after that catalog is in hand should code paths be considered.
rules.why: Session #71 (2026-05-08): For SEPA_CT V001 Dbtr structured-address I proposed three code paths (Custom Z FM Z_DMEE_DBTR_HQ_STREET reading T001->ADRC; BAdI extension to YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_DEBIT; speculative empirical AUSTO test) before reading the SAP-std SEPA_CT format tree from Note 0001798463 (file SEPA_CT_260916.XML on disk in the user's Downloads folder). When Pablo pushed back ('this information is not custom, some standard function for SEPA should cover it'), parsing that XML revealed that SAP ships FPAYHX-AUSTO + FPAYHX-AUST3 as paying-co AdrLine sources AND that UNESCO already has FPAYHX-ZPFST/ZPLOR/ZLISO as purpose-built Z-extensions on the header buffer. DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET on FPAYHX in D01 confirmed all 7 fields exist with appropriate lengths (ZPFST=35 'P.O. Box or Street for Postal Code/City'; ZPLOR=46 'Postal Code/City of the Payee'; ZLISO=2 ISO country). The 'invent code' path was a 30-LOC + transport waste; the SAP-std answer was a config-only rebind. Cost of the wrong proposal: one extra back-and-forth and Pablo's correction. Cost prevented going forward: future agents proposing custom Z-objects for problems SAP solved 15 years ago.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Whenever the user mentions a DMEE format that has an SAP Note (SEPA_CT 0001798463; SEPA_DD 0001798463 same note; CGI varies by release; CITI proprietary so this rule N/A), check the user's Downloads / artifact folders for the format XML before any design proposal. (2) Parse the format XML for the leaf in question — list every Element with that <Name> and dump MappingProcedure / TableName / FieldName / ExitFunction / Constant / Condition. Multiple Element occurrences usually mean multiple bindings under different parents (Dbtr/Cdtr/UltmtDbtr) or different conditional branches. (3) Distinguish header-buffer (FPAYHX, paying-co context) vs line-buffer (FPAYH/FPAYP, vendor context) sources. Structured leaves under Dbtr need FPAYHX; under Cdtr need FPAYH (per-line) or FPAYP (item). (4) Run DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET on the buffer table in D01 to confirm the field exists + its length + domain — gives ground truth. Use Zagentexecution/mcp-backend-server-python/extract_fpayhx_field_catalog.py as template. (5) Only after step 4 fails (no SAP-std field, no customer Z-ext, exit module needed) should code paths be considered. (6) Document the SAP-std bindings in the change matrix CSV with a 'sap_std_source' column citing the XML Element index for traceability.

rules.rule: Before binding a DMEE leaf to any FPAYHX or FPAYH field (especially UNESCO Z-extensions like ZPFST, ZPLOR, ZLISO, ZSTRA, ZBSTR, ZBORT), walk the tree from the leaf's NODE_ID up to the nearest Dbtr/Cdtr/UltmtDbtr/UltmtCdtr/InitgPty ancestor in the EXTRACTED tree (dmee_tree_node_p01.csv via PARENT_ID chain) to identify the leaf's CONTEXT. The Z-prefix on UNESCO append-structure fields does NOT signal paying-co context - those Z-extensions can be populated with either Cdtr (per-line vendor) or Dbtr (paying-co) data depending on the runtime populator. Production V000 active version is the only authoritative source.
rules.why: Session #71 (2026-05-08): For SEPA Dbtr V001 design I made TWO wrong revisions before getting it right. Revision #1 proposed binding StrtNm to FPAYHX/REF01 + CM005/OBPM3 register (cross-format coupling, REF01 is CGI/CITI architecture). Revision #2 proposed FPAYHX-ZPFST/ZPLOR/ZLISO claiming they were paying-co Z-extensions (DDIF text 'P.O. Box or Street for Postal Code/City of Payee's Display' was misread as 'paying-co' - actually 'Payee' = recipient = vendor). The correct verdict came from grep'ing dmee_tree_node_p01.csv: PARENT N_4754354180 of ZPFST/ZPLOR/ZLISO bindings has TECH_NAME = PstlAdr under Cdtr (vendor), confirming these are per-line vendor-context Z-extensions. Production V000 paying-co Dbtr uses ORT1Z + LAND1 + AUST1 + NAMEZ; for StrtNm/PstCd structured no FPAYHX field exists, so UNESCO's canonical pattern is BAdI extension via FI_CGI_DMEE_EXIT_W_BADI -> YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT (used for both Cdtr and Dbtr). The cost of getting context wrong: each revision burns one user back-and-forth and risks transporting a config that renders vendor data under Dbtr (the original 2026-05-07 bug).
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When asked which FPAYHX/FPAYH field to bind a Dbtr/Cdtr/Ultmt* leaf to, FIRST identify production V000 active version's existing bindings under that exact ancestor: grep dmee_tree_node_p01.csv for the ancestor's NODE_ID, list all FPAYHX/FPAYH children, note their TECH_NAME and FIELDNAME. (2) Trace the leaf's PARENT_ID chain upward until hitting Dbtr/Cdtr/UltmtDbtr/UltmtCdtr/InitgPty - that's the context. (3) Verify the field's runtime semantic by reading SAP-std code that POPULATES it (CL_IDFI_CGI_CALL05_GENERIC_CM005, SAPFPAYM, BTE handlers) - field text alone is unreliable (DDIF descriptions are often misleading; 'Payee' might mean Cdtr OR Dbtr depending on author intent). (4) If no FPAYHX/FPAYH field carries the right context, default to UNESCO's canonical BAdI pattern: bind leaf with EXIT_FUNC=FI_CGI_DMEE_EXIT_W_BADI and add a WHEN i_node_path case to YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT method (handles both credit and debit branches per FLT_VAL_DEBIT_OR_CREDIT). (5) Document context+evidence in matrix CSV EVIDENCE_ANCHOR column with the dmee_tree_node_p01.csv line number and the nearest ancestor's TECH_NAME.

rules.rule: Before designing or transporting any V001 (or V00x) extension to a DMEE payment medium format tree, verify the format's SAP lifecycle status: open tx OBPM1 / SE16 TFPM (table for PMW formats) / search SAP Notes for 'obsolete <format_name>'. SAP marks formats as obsolete when they are superseded (e.g. SEPA_CT replaced by CGI_XML_CT per message BFIBL02591). Building V001 against an obsolete format burns transports + ABAP review cycles on a dead-end format that SAP Support will not fix.
rules.why: Session #71 (2026-05-08): Pablo discovered SAP message BFIBL02591 declaring SEPA_CT obsolete (replacement: CGI_XML_CT) AFTER 4 sessions of V001 SEPA design work, including 3 wrong revisions, 81-scenario test corpus planning, OBPM3 register decisions, BAdI extension drafts, and DDIF inspections. None of this would have been wasted if the format lifecycle had been the FIRST check: extending SEPA_CT V001 means enhancing a format SAP no longer maintains, with no SAP-Support escalation path post-CBPR+ deadline. The correct strategic move is migrate the SocGen rail to CGI_XML_CT (UNESCO already has /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO operating; V9 is the SAP-std reference). Cost of wrong order: ~4-5 sessions of effort on the dead tree before the lifecycle gate triggered.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) On day 1 of any DMEE format work, run: SE16 TFPM where FORMI = '<format_name>' or check tx OBPM1; look for STATUS or OBSOLETE flag and tooltips. (2) Search SAP Notes / SAP Help Portal for 'BFIBL02591' or 'obsolete <format>' text. (3) If user has F_SHOW_OBSOLETE_TFPM=X parameter set, the format will still appear in dropdowns - that's an indicator it might be obsolete. (4) If format is obsolete: STOP. The replacement format (per SAP message diagnosis line) is the new build target. Update plan documents and matrix CSV before any further design work. (5) Document the decision in plan: 'Format X is OBSOLETE per SAP Note <id>, replaced by Y. Migrating SocGen / CITI / etc. payment method assignments from X to Y in FBZP.' (6) Build the V001 against the replacement, not the obsolete original.

rules.rule: Before writing WHEN clauses in YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT (or any country variant) to handle a new DMEE tag, FIRST check whether the UNESCO PPC framework (YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_UTIL.GET_TAG_VALUE_FROM_CUSTO + YTFI_PPC_TAG + YTFI_PPC_STRUC) already covers the requirement via Z-table config. The PPC framework was built by N_MENARD 2024-09-06 specifically as the config-driven dispatcher for tag-value resolution: domains YD_FI_PPC_CODE (5 values: SEPARATOR/FIXED_VAL/PPC_VAR/PPC_DESCR/PAY_FIELD) + YD_FI_PAY_STRUC (FPAYH/FPAYHX/FPAYP). New DMEE tags activated for any country should be added as Z-table rows (YTFI_PPC_TAG entry mapping LAND1+DEB_CRE+TAG_FULL to TAG_ID; YTFI_PPC_STRUC entries with PPC_CODE rules) — not as ABAP WHEN clauses. Only when the existing PPC_CODE values cannot resolve the value (e.g. need ADRC read for paying-co address, no FPAYH-Z field populated) should ABAP delta be considered, and the delta should EXTEND the PPC framework (new PPC_CODE in domain YD_FI_PPC_CODE + UTIL.CM003 case) — never bypass it with bespoke WHEN clauses in FALLBACK_CM001.
rules.why: Session #71 (2026-05-08): For V001 SEPA Dbtr structured-address I proposed extending YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT with 3-4 WHEN clauses reading ADRC via T001-ADRNR (~30 LOC). Pablo pointed out 'we have YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_UTIL', revealing that UNESCO already has the canonical config-driven framework I should have used. Brain claims 76/97/98 (sessions #62) had documented this PPC framework completely (11+133 rows, schema, domains, entry point CM002, retrofit gap) but I didn't traverse those claims when designing. Result: my proposed bespoke BAdI WHEN-clause approach would have created an architectural inconsistency — UNESCO uses PPC config-driven everywhere except this new code path. The correct pattern is: new DMEE tag activation = Z-table rows (8 rows for 4 leaves x 2 tables), and ABAP delta only when the PPC_CODE vocabulary needs extension (~10 LOC + 1 DDIC domain row, vs ~30 LOC of WHEN clauses). The cost of getting this wrong without Pablo catching it: bespoke ABAP code that future maintainers can't extend via config.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When asked to handle a new DMEE tag value, first check brain_v2/claims/claims.json for 'PPC' or 'YTFI_PPC_TAG' to see existing framework documentation. (2) Read YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_UTIL_CM003 to see the dispatcher logic. (3) Check YTFI_PPC_TAG and YTFI_PPC_STRUC current rows via Gold DB query (`SELECT * FROM YTFI_PPC_TAG WHERE LAND1='<co_iso>'`) to see what's configured. (4) Determine if existing PPC_CODE vocabulary (SEPARATOR/FIXED_VAL/PPC_VAR/PPC_DESCR/PAY_FIELD with PAY_STRUC=FPAYH/FPAYHX/FPAYP) can resolve the value with config alone. (5) If yes → propose Z-table rows (no ABAP). (6) If no → propose new PPC_CODE in domain YD_FI_PPC_CODE + 1 case in UTIL.CM003 (~10 LOC). (7) NEVER write WHEN clauses in FALLBACK_CM001 GET_CREDIT for tag value resolution — that method's role is name-overflow handling and edge cases, not config dispatch. (8) Document the proposed Z-table rows in matrix CSV with explicit PPC_CODE/PAY_STRUC/PAY_FIELD/PPC_VALUE columns for SM30 / transport.

rules.rule: INSERT REPORT on a function-group include (e.g. LYFPAYMU19) DESTROYS the FUPARAREF interface metadata for the function modules in that include. After every INSERT REPORT on such an include, ALWAYS execute `GENERATE REPORT '<FUNCTION_GROUP>'` (e.g. SAPLYFPAYM) in the same one-shot to repopulate FUPARAREF.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): deployed Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v2 via INSERT REPORT on LYFPAYMU19. The FM source updated correctly (REPOSRC R3STATE='A'), but FUPARAREF returned TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA — interface metadata was wiped. Symptoms: RPY_FUNCTIONMODULE_READ_NEW returns 0 lines; DMEE editor reports DMEE_ABA358 'incorrect interface'; FM may execute partially (cached compiled code) or fail silently per call. The fix was an explicit `GENERATE REPORT 'SAPLYFPAYM'` which restored 11 FUPARAREF rows from the `*"` interface comments in the source.
rules.how_to_apply:
Whenever updating a function-module body via INSERT REPORT on its include:
1. INSERT REPORT 'L<FG>U<NN>' FROM lt_src DIRECTORY ENTRY ls_trdir.
2. COMMIT WORK.
3. GENERATE REPORT 'SAPL<FG>' MESSAGE lv_msg.
4. Verify: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — should be > 0.
5. If still empty, the GENERATE failed silently — investigate before assuming the FM is OK.
The RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN one-shot must include both INSERT and GENERATE in one program so they execute under the same transaction.

rules.rule: `GENERATE REPORT '<FG>'` regenerates the function-group code BUT does NOT re-parse the `*"` interface comments to update existing FUPARAREF rows. To change a parameter's pass-by-reference flag (VALUE→REFERENCE or vice versa), you must `UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...` directly via ABAP one-shot, then GENERATE again.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): edited Y_FI_DMEE_ADR `*"` comments to change `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` → `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)` (matching DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA). Deployed via INSERT REPORT + GENERATE REPORT. FUPARAREF still showed `reference=' '` (blank=VALUE) for I_EXTENSION. DMEE_ABA358 errors persisted. Fix: explicit UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname='Y_FI_DMEE_ADR' AND parameter='I_EXTENSION'. Then re-GENERATE. The errors disappeared.
rules.how_to_apply:
When changing FM interface in `*"` comments (pass-by-value vs reference, optional flag, type, structure):
1. Edit the source `*"` comments and INSERT REPORT.
2. GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' (regenerates code but NOT FUPARAREF flags).
3. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — verify each parameter's `reference`, `optional`, `structure` matches the new comments.
4. For any mismatch, UPDATE fupararef SET <flag>='<new>' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...
5. COMMIT WORK + GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' again.
6. Re-verify FUPARAREF and run the FM via SE37 or actual caller to confirm.
Key FUPARAREF columns: PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE (I/E/C/T), STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION, R3STATE.

rules.rule: DMEE exit function modules (those configured as MP_EXIT_FUNC in DMEE_TREE_NODE) MUST have an interface that EXACTLY matches one of the two SAP templates: DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_ABA (legacy) or DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA (modern, with REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)). Any deviation triggers DMEE_ABA358 'function module XXX has incorrect interface' and the tree validation refuses to compile.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR had `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` while DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA has `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)`. The mismatch produced 8 DMEE_ABA358 errors (one per Dbtr/PstlAdr/* leaf assigned to Y_FI_DMEE_ADR). Runtime sometimes tolerates the mismatch (executes with a cached compile), but tree-editor validation, transport activation, and Test mode all reject. Strict-match is enforced field-by-field in FUPARAREF: parameter name, paramtype (I/E/C/T), structure, reference flag, optional flag, position.
rules.how_to_apply:
Before assigning a custom FM as a DMEE node exit:
1. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA' (the reference).
2. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='<your custom FM>'.
3. Diff the two: every field — PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE, STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION — must match.
4. If mismatch, fix via INSERT REPORT (source comments) + UPDATE fupararef (reference flag) + GENERATE REPORT.
5. Test by running tx DMEE → tree → Validate / Test active version. Should be zero DMEE_ABA358.
Reference template (extended): `IMPORTING VALUE(I_TREE_TYPE) TYPE DMEE_TREETYPE_ABA, VALUE(I_TREE_ID) TYPE DMEE_TREEID_ABA, VALUE(I_ITEM), VALUE(I_PARAM), VALUE(I_UPARAM), REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION) TYPE DMEE_EXIT_INTERFACE_ABA. EXPORTING REFERENCE(O_VALUE), REFERENCE(C_VALUE), REFERENCE(N_VALUE), REFERENCE(P_VALUE). TABLES I_TAB.`

rules.rule: Every piece of code we extract from SAP (ABAP source via RPY_PROGRAM_READ, function modules, classes, includes, enhancements, BAdI implementations, BTEs) is BRAIN DATA — not transient artifacts. It must be persisted under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/, registered in brain_v2 (annotations, claims, knowledge_docs), and linked in brain_state.json so future agents can: (1) understand how SAP works at UNESCO, (2) detect patterns across modules, (3) discover connections between elements and domains, (4) avoid re-extracting the same code, (5) audit historical SAP behavior.
rules.why: User directive Session #073 (2026-05-09): 'Y las bajadas de codigo son datos que deben estar en el brain para conocer como funciona SAP luego los agentes determinan patrones y conexiones entre elementos y domains'. The raison d'etre of the brain v2 backbone (rule feedback_brain_code_tables_are_backbone) is that programs+tables+config are the SAP system, and edges between them are the intelligence. Extracted code is the only way to make those edges concrete (code → reads_table → joins_with). If extracted code only lives as one-off files outside the brain, every analysis starts from scratch. Concrete pain Session #073: while studying Nicolas's YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK / FR / DE / IT / UTIL classes, I discovered a sophisticated PPC-customizing pattern (YTFI_PPC_TAG + YTFI_PPC_STRUC + T015L driven by util class constructor) that should be a brain-level annotation visible to every future incident touching DMEE — otherwise the next agent re-discovers it from scratch.
rules.how_to_apply:
On every code extraction:
1. Save source under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/<NAME>.abap (e.g. extracted_code/FI/DMEE_p01_canonical/YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK====CM001.abap).
2. For each new object: add an annotation to brain_v2/annotations/annotations.json with finding (1-2 sentences of what the code does), tag, flavor, related_objects, evidence_tier=TIER_1 source code, line numbers if specific.
3. For patterns spanning multiple objects: write a knowledge doc under knowledge/domains/<DOMAIN>/ and link it from the relevant brain_state.objects[X].knowledge_docs.
4. For author/team-ownership: capture in annotation 'author' field (e.g. 'N_MENARD') so future agents respect feedback_only_modify_our_own_code.
5. Run brain_v2/rebuild_all.py at session close to refresh brain_state.json.
6. Cross-reference: when extracting object X, check brain_state.objects[X] first — if already annotated, only add new findings, do not duplicate.
7. NEVER let extracted_code/ rot — it is a first-class persistence layer of the project.

rules.rule: Rule: when emitting a vendor address from any UNESCO output (DMEE, avisos, F110 confirms, BCM print, treasury report), check PA0006 SUBTY='1' BEFORE reading ADRC.STREET. Cast LIFNR → PERNR via NUMC(8). If PA0006 hits → employee path (real home address). If not → vendor path (ADRC). The dispatch is KTOKK-agnostic — explicit KTOKK='SCSA' branching (the v5 design) misses cases where staff are paid against KTOKK=UNES / INDV / ICVS LIFNRs.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-08): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v5 used explicit KTOKK='SCSA' detection. F110 SEPA run for Simona BERTOLDINI emitted 'BFM/FAS/PAY' as <StrtNm> because her payment LIFNR is KTOKK=UNES (not SCSA), so v5 fell through to ADRC and printed the dept code. v6 PA0006-first detection is robust regardless of which KTOKK F110 paid against. Validated live on D01 V01T3 run — BERTOLDINI's real home address (16 avenue des Murs du Parc, 94300 Vincennes) emitted correctly. UNESCO LIFNR↔PERNR convention: PERNR = LIFNR cast NUMC(8) (e.g. 0010008305 → 10008305). ADRC.STREET stores dept codes for SCSA staff records — assuming ADRC = real address is wrong system-wide, not just SEPA-specific.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) For any new code that emits a vendor address: SELECT SINGLE FROM PA0006 WHERE PERNR = LIFNR (NUMC8 cast) AND SUBTY='1' AND date-valid first. (2) If SY-SUBRC=0 → use PA0006-STRAS/PSTLZ/ORT01/LAND1/STATE. (3) Else fall back to ADRC of the LIFNR. (4) For audit of EXISTING code: grep for SELECT * FROM ADRC patterns where the addrnumber comes from LIFNR-related sources (LFA1-ADRNR, FPAYH-ZADNR, etc.) — every such site is a candidate for the same bug. (5) Document the convention in the affected output's spec / companion. (6) Reference: Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v6 in extracted_code/FI/DMEE_full_inventory/Y_FI_DMEE_ADR_v6.abap; knowledge/domains/Payment/vendor_address_routing_by_ktokk.md.

rules.rule: Before claiming a custom FM (e.g. Y_FI_DMEE_ADR) fixes a payment-format bug, query DMEE_TREE_NODE.MP_EXIT_FUNC for every relevant tree to confirm the FM is actually wired. A fix only applies where the tree calls it.
rules.why: Session #074: I initially extended the v6 simulator across all SEPA formats — but Y_FI_DMEE_ADR is wired ONLY in /SEPA_CT_UNES. The drift forecast for /SEPA_CT_ICTP_* was theoretical (would-happen-if), not in-scope. User caught this: 'no cambien nunca estos formatos cómo puede ser que funcione'. The same logic applies to /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO and /CITI/XML/UNESCO/DC_V3_01 — they wire FI_CGI_DMEE_EXIT_W_BADI and /CITIPMW/* FMs, not Y_FI_DMEE_ADR. The fix surface is bounded by tree wiring, not by FM availability.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) For any payment-format bug claim, query DMEE_TREE_NODE for the affected leaves with MP_EXIT_FUNC populated. (2) Separate 'in-scope' (FM is wired) from 'theoretical' (FM would fix if wired). (3) When reporting drift across formats, label each row as IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE based on tree wiring evidence, not on assumed coverage. (4) Reference: extracted DMEE_TREE_NODE topology for the 5 active formats in claim 185.

rules.rule: DFPAYG (execution evidence) and DFPAYV (config matrix) are the canonical source for any 'which payment format/run/vendor' question. Always cross-reference both before answering scope or coverage questions about UNESCO payments.
rules.why: Session #074 added both tables to Gold DB. DFPAYG = 9,848 rows = ground truth for what actually fired in the last 2 years; DFPAYV = 84 rows = static config showing what CAN fire (with 6 lapsed configs that never run). Combined with REGUH, they let SQL answer: 'which staff vendor was paid via which format×cocode×bank×account×PM combination?' — replacing ad-hoc P01 RFC queries.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Format scope questions: SELECT DISTINCT FORMI FROM DFPAYG WHERE LAUFD >= '<window>' (= active set); SELECT FORMI FROM DFPAYV (= configured set); difference = lapsed configs. (2) Vendor questions: JOIN DFPAYG to REGUH on (LAUFD, LAUFI, ZBUKR) to get the vendor list paid via each format. (3) Bank/account/PM granularity: REGUH_FAST has HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE — better than DFPAYG for the routing breakdown. (4) Indexes: idx_reguh_run on (LAUFD,LAUFI,ZBUKR), idx_dfpayg_formi, idx_dfpayg_zbukr.

rules.rule: When reporting payment metrics, ALWAYS label whether the count is 'distinct LIFNRs' or 'REGUH payment lines'. Same employee paid 30 times = 1 distinct LIFNR = 30 lines. The two scales differ by 5-30x in typical UNESCO data.
rules.why: Session #074 user clarification: 'O sea son la cantidades de pagos staff que se hacen para ese formato' — user assumed 'staff drift = number of payments' but my number was 'distinct staff vendors'. The actual XMLs emitted = REGUH lines, not vendors. For /SEPA_CT_UNES UNES 2025-26: 1,659 staff vendors but 12,107 lines (7.3x factor).
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Default to BOTH counts when reporting: e.g. '1,659 staff vendors → 12,107 lines'. (2) For business impact (XMLs emitted with wrong data, bank rejection volume), use LINES. (3) For root-cause analysis (which employees are affected), use VENDORS. (4) Include the multiplier explicitly: 'pays/vendor ratio = 7.3x'.

rules.rule: When presenting tables to operational users, use the FULL business name for each column (Company Code, House Bank, Bank Account, Payment Method) — NOT the SAP technical abbreviation (ZBUKR, HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE) or my shorthand (COCO, BANK, ACCT, PM).
rules.why: Session #074 user feedback: 'O faltan las columnas, Company code, house bank bank Account, and mediunm payment please' — when I used abbreviated headers, the user explicitly asked for the full names. Treasury and finance operators read SAP tables every day but the technical names slow them down vs business labels.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) First column header row uses business names: 'Company Code (ZBUKR)' is acceptable, 'ZBUKR' alone is not. (2) Apply consistently across companions and brain output. (3) Exception: when the audience is purely technical (ABAP devs / brain agents), abbreviations are fine.

rules.rule: RFC_READ_TABLE has narrow accepted OPTIONS syntax: (a) NO 'IN (...)' clauses — use multiple single-field calls instead; (b) leading space required when concatenating conditions (' AND TECH_NAME = ...'); (c) DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED on wide tables — limit FIELDS to <20 columns or expect 512-byte WA truncation. Document tables that are DMEE_TREE_NODE, REGUH, etc. often hit these limits.
rules.why: Session #074 wasted ~15 minutes debugging OPTION_NOT_VALID errors when querying DMEE_TREE_NODE with IN clauses. Once switched to per-TECH_NAME calls in a loop, queries worked. This is a recurring pattern across sessions but never captured as a rule.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When OPTION_NOT_VALID appears, simplify OPTIONS: one condition per row, leading space on continuation rows, no IN clauses. (2) For multi-value filtering, loop the query per value instead. (3) When DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED hits, narrow FIELDS list or split into multiple narrow queries. (4) Verified working pattern: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID = '/X'"}, {'TEXT':" AND TECH_NAME = 'StrtNm'"}]. Bad: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID='/X' AND TECH_NAME IN ('StrtNm','BldgNb')"}].

rules.rule: When SAP auth fails, ALWAYS test the same credentials via both RFC (port 3300) AND HTTP (port 80) before declaring 'password is wrong'. SAP commonly accepts the same user/password on one protocol while rejecting it on another — caused by SU01 user type, USR02 password-buffer desync, or SICF policy. Run the 60-second diagnostic in unescrp/.claude/skills/sap-fiori-react-builder/sap-fiori-react-builder/references/deployment/sap-d01-connection-patterns.md before opening a credentials INC.
rules.why: Session #075: unescrp project burned 2+ hours assuming the 40-char password was stale, including retrying passwords found in earlier .env snapshots and probing /sap/bc/adt/discovery 6 times. The same password authenticates cleanly via RFC. Root cause is SAP-side ICF/SU01 — none of the client-side fixes would have helped. Isolating protocol vs credentials would have saved the time and triggered the correct BASIS ticket immediately.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) First failure to authenticate → run RFC probe (pyrfc T000 read). (2) If RFC works → it's not the password; switch to HTTP probe (urllib Basic + ADT discovery). (3) If RFC fails → check .env / VPN / SNC config. (4) If RFC works AND HTTP fails → SAP-side, open BASIS ticket with the diagnostic evidence. Don't keep trying passwords. (5) Document the result in the project's connection-patterns reference file.

rules.rule: Do NOT trust `sap_adt_client.fetch_csrf()` or any `_request()` call as proof of HTTP auth success. The current `_request` implementation catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and returns `(status, body, headers)` without raising — and SAP echoes a CSRF token even on 401 when `X-CSRF-Token: Fetch` is sent. Always assert `status == 200` after the call. Patch `_request()` to raise on 4xx, or replace the client with one that propagates errors.
rules.why: Session #075: I told the user 'ADT HTTP works' based on `fetch_csrf()` returning normally, then realized the client silently swallowed the 401 and returned an empty token. The mistake cost trust and required a public correction. The bug has likely caused false positives in other sessions where ADT 'success' messages preceded mysterious downstream failures.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When calling sap_adt_client methods, check the returned status code explicitly, not just whether a value came back. (2) Add a fix to `_request`: `if status >= 400: raise HTTPError(...)`. (3) Same patch needed for fetch_csrf, search_object, get_source, etc. (4) Until patched, run a separate `urllib.request.urlopen` probe to confirm 200 before trusting the client.

rules.rule: When another project (Tier 2 application or sibling Tier 1) consumes this brain, SAP-system facts (tables, transactions, standard customizing, customer customizing in any SAP module) MUST live ONLY in abapobjectscreation/brain_v2. The consuming project cites by reference (path + node id) and never duplicates. Project-specific facts (Z objects the consumer is building, design decisions, application-internal taxonomy) live in the consumer's brain.
rules.why: Session #00 of FINCLOSSING (2026-05-23) — first Tier 2 application project that needs to consume SAP truth without forking it. Without this rule, two brains will diverge on facts like 'BKPF columns' or 'CLOCO table layout' and the failure mode (silent drift) is invisible until an agent makes a wrong decision against a stale copy. Plausibility-without-evidence (CP-003 violation) is the concrete failure pattern.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Before writing a fact to a consumer's brain, ask: 'is this about SAP itself, or about what the consumer is BUILDING?' (2) If about SAP → grep abapobjectscreation/brain_v2 first; if missing, ADD it to abapobjectscreation, not the consumer. (3) If about the consumer's Z objects / design / app-internal taxonomy → consumer's brain is correct. (4) Each consumer maintains a `refs_external.json` listing every layer/file it reads from this brain — that is the canonical drift-detection surface. (5) Reverse pointer: this brain maintains `brain_v2/consumers.md` listing every project that depends on it, so refactors here check downstream impact.

rules.rule: When prior analysis has converged on an obvious recommended path AND the user signals agreement (OK/si/dale/proceed), do NOT present a 3-option AskUserQuestion menu. Execute the recommendation directly. The agent OWNS the technical decision.
rules.why: During session #076 ADT expansion, after a long analysis that converged on Build now + BASIS ticket in parallel, I still presented a 3-option menu. User rejected the tool use and said OK proceed im not sure what you need from basis. Menus are friction when path is obvious. Reinforces existing rule feedback_own_the_decision_stop_asking.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. If my prior message ended with clear recommendation + user agrees (OK/si/dale/proceed), do not present options. Execute.
2. Reserve AskUserQuestion for genuinely-equivalent-tradeoff cases or when user has not yet given any signal.
3. When the user signals lack of context (not sure what X means), do NOT ask them to choose - give them what they need or just decide for them and explain.
4. If I find myself drafting an AskUserQuestion after a long analysis, delete it and proceed.

rules.rule: Before recommending any SAP capability (ADT endpoint, BAPI, RFC FM, transaction availability), VERIFY it exists on the target kernel via empirical probe. SAP NetWeaver capabilities differ across releases - what works in S/4HANA / NW 7.5x may be 404 on UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 (NW 7.40). Never assume kernel-uniform.
rules.why: Session #076 violation: I confidently recommended ADT REST define_table / create_index as the canonical DDIC path, including copy-paste prompts for the parallel unescrp conversation. Then user tested empirically and confirmed /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on D01 (NW 7.40) - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. ~400 lines of code became S/4HANA scaffolding, cross-project recommendation had to be retracted before being applied.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Before recommending an ADT method, call adt_discovery() and grep the response for the relevant collection. If endpoint absent, the method will 404 - recommend RFC alternative instead.
2. Before recommending a BAPI / RFC FM, run RFC_READ_TABLE FROM TFDIR WHERE FUNCNAME EQ name to confirm availability.
3. Before recommending a transaction, verify via TSTCT or quick GUI probe.
4. UNESCO landscape baseline: ECC 6.0 EhP8 = NW 7.40. Treat any capability described as NW 7.5+ or S/4HANA-only as unavailable until proven otherwise.
5. When recommending a path that crosses kernel versions, be explicit about version requirement IN THE RECOMMENDATION.
6. When a recommendation is later proven wrong by empirical evidence, revise the related memory rules IMMEDIATELY and acknowledge the error directly - no softening.

rules.rule: For ANY new ABAP/DDIC object work (create table, DE, domain, class, program, FM, index, etc.), the agent works EXCLUSIVELY in D01. NEVER touches P01 - not for write, not for read, not for preflight, not for does this exist. The only legitimate P01 read in a creation context is post-transport verification.
rules.why: Session #076 violation: I called from_env(P01) and ran RFC_READ_TABLE FROM DD02L WHERE TABNAME='ZCRP_CERTHEAD' to triple-confirm the table doesn't exist there. The check was logically unnecessary - by the transport model, if it doesn't exist in D01 it cannot exist in P01 - and crossed a boundary the user explicitly maintains. User response in CAPS: PARA NUEVOS OBJETOS LO HACEMOS EN D01!!! NUNCA P01. This rule is STRICTER than the broader no-prod-writes rule.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. When the user mentions creating/modifying/deploying a new ABAP/DDIC object: pin the system as D01 only. Do not call from_env(P01).
2. For preflight of objects related to a new creation, query D01 only.
3. The only legitimate P01 read in a new-object context is post-transport verification - prefer STMS over RFC.
4. If user explicitly requests a P01 probe for some OTHER reason (incident, data extraction, customizing read), that is allowed under standard no-prod-writes rule.
5. If unsure whether request is new-object work or diagnosis work, ASK before touching P01.

rules.rule: ADT-first is qualified by kernel + object class. SOURCE CODE objects (PROG/CLAS/INTF/FUGR/FUNC/INCLUDE/ENHO/XSLT/BSP) - ADT-first on ALL kernels including EhP8. DDIC objects (TABL/DTEL/DOMA/INDX) - ADT-first ONLY on NW 7.50+ / S/4HANA. On EhP8 (UNESCO D01/P01) DDIC creation MUST use the DDIF wrapper (sap_adt_client.define_table_via_ddif / define_data_element_via_ddif / define_domain_via_ddif) with TR_TADIR_INTERFACE injection and verify_tadir post-check.
rules.why: Session #076: I originally saved a rule ADT-first for ALL DDIC, generating ABAP programs that call DDIF_*_PUT is forbidden as architecture. Empirical probe revealed ADT REST /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on NW 7.40 - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. So on EhP8 the DDIF_*_PUT via RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN pattern is NOT debt - it is the only path. Pain points (opaque RC=2, IN-list parser bug, TADIR-orphan) are real and mitigated by the wrapper, not avoided. The original rule overgeneralized and had to be corrected.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Before any DDIC create/modify, call adt_discovery() once and grep for the endpoint. If absent, fall back to the DDIF wrapper (NEVER to ad-hoc programs without preflight + TADIR fix).
2. For SOURCE CODE work, default to ADT REST.
3. When reviewing legacy projects for RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN + DDIF_*_PUT patterns on EhP8, do NOT mark them as debt - verify they implement preflight + TR_TADIR_INTERFACE + structured-error mitigation. If they do, the pattern is correct; if not, refactor to the wrapper, do not switch to ADT (which would fail).
4. Track the S/4HANA migration: when UNESCO upgrades, flip DDIC operations to the ADT methods (already scaffolded) - field-list and return-dict shape are identical.
5. DDIC creation order (both paths): Domain - Data Element - Table - Index. Validate prerequisites before each create.

rules.rule: CRITICAL HARD RULE: NEVER modify, alter, extend the structure of, append fields to, change DEs of, or alter activation state of SAP-delivered standard objects. Applies to ALL tools (DDIF wrapper, ADT REST, abapGit pull, RFC FM calls, Playwright). Only Z*/Y*/customer-namespace objects can be modified. For SAP-standard extension needs, use append structures, customer includes, BAdIs, enhancement implementations, or user exits — never modify the original. Refuse the request and explain when asked to modify a standard object.
rules.why: SAP licensing forbids unauthorized modification of delivered objects (SSCR keys required); upgrades (SPS/EhP/S/4HANA conversion) overwrite standard objects and force SPDD/SPAU manual adjustments which are manual, error-prone, and break frequently. UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 is a mature production estate where standard modifications carry ongoing maintenance cost on every Support Package application — UNESCO BASIS team will refuse them on principle. Modifying a standard DE/domain cascades activation to thousands of dependent tables. A wrong TR_TADIR_INTERFACE call against a standard object can set EDTFLAG=X and break SE11 editability system-wide.
rules.how_to_apply:
Before any DDIC/code write: check if object name is non-standard.

  def is_standard(name): return not name.upper().startswith(('Z','Y','/'))

If standard, REFUSE the call and respond:
  1. Cite this rule (feedback_never_modify_standard_objects)
  2. Explain why (SAP licensing + upgrade safety + UNESCO policy)
  3. Offer permitted alternative (append structure / customer include / BAdI / enhancement)
  4. Ask user to rephrase as Z-namespace addition

Permitted alternatives:
  - Add fields to standard table: Z append structure (CI_* include or .APPEND)
  - Modify standard FM behavior: BAdI / enhancement spot / user exit (Z implementation)
  - Modify standard class behavior: ENHO enhancement implementation
  - Customizing of standard T-tables: SM30 row CRUD = DATA changes (permitted), structure changes (forbidden)

Edge cases:
  - Customizing rows in T-tables: data changes are OK, structure changes are NOT
  - PFCG role modifications: copy to Z-named role first
  - SICF service activation: flag toggle OK; handler class modification NOT

rules.rule: ARCHITECTURAL STANDARD: abapGit is the DEFAULT deployment path for any object type it supports (170+ types covering DDIC, source code, enhancements, OData, BSP). DDIF wrapper / ADT REST / RFC alternatives are BRIDGES or FALLBACKS for cases abapGit cannot cover OR for the period until abapGit is installed on the target system. Priority order: 1) abapGit (default for supported types when installed), 2) ADT REST (source code on all kernels, bridge for source until abapGit), 3) DDIF wrapper (DDIC on EhP8, bridge until abapGit), 4) RFC/Playwright (for objects no other tool covers: SM59, SM30 rows, SICF, RZ10, BOR, PFCG user assignments).
rules.why: abapGit is the de-facto industry standard for SAP Z code deployment: 10+ years, 50K+ installs, SAP-promoted via TechEd. It handles TADIR/CTS architecturally correctly (uses RS_CORR_INSERT, no EDTFLAG bug), provides native version control with Git history/blame/diff/rollback, supports atomic multi-object deploys (N objects in 1 ZIP = 1 TR), is forward-compatible across kernels (EhP8/NW 7.5x/S/4HANA), enables cross-system sync (D01->QAS without STMS forward path), and supports PR-based code review. The DDIF wrapper we built is a hand-rolled subset that learned the same lessons through bugs (TADIR-orphan, EDTFLAG poisoning) that abapGit solves by design. Installation operational state (installed or not) is separate from architectural correctness (abapGit IS the standard regardless).
rules.how_to_apply:
When proposing a deployment: lead with "if abapGit is installed, use it; otherwise the bridge is X". Don't propose the bridge as the default.

When abapGit is not installed (current D01 state): include the BASIS ticket escalation in the response, marked STRATEGIC PRIORITY (not optional). Bridge solution is temporary.

When designing new automation: API shape compatible with both backends (e.g. define_table(...) works whether backend is abapGit-pull or DDIF wrapper). Forward-compatible.

When migrating to S/4HANA: abapGit path stays. DDIF wrapper deprecates. ADT REST takes over what DDIF did, but abapGit lifecycle features remain its own value.

When auditing legacy projects (unescrp, ecosystem): check if they use abapGit. If yes, validate they're using it correctly. If no, propose migration when timing allows.

Before recommending abapGit as the immediate path: verify install via 5-way TADIR/TRDIR/TDEVC/TFDIR probe (per feedback_verify_capabilities_before_recommending). If not installed, recommend bridge with STRATEGIC install ticket attached.

rules.rule: When assessing whether a SAP data-access restriction (note, patch, audit, security advisory) affects us, FIRST read our code to classify the EXACT function-module / API family our pipeline calls, then compare it against the SPECIFIC API the restriction names. Never reason from the category ('it is an RFC that reads data'). ODP Data Replication APIs (RODPS_REPL_*, ODQ_*, /SAPDS/) are a different framework from the generic RFC_READ_TABLE reader. UNESCO's Gold DB uses RFC_READ_TABLE only and is OUT OF SCOPE of SAP Note 3255746; the 2026-06-09 ODP-blocking patch does not affect it.
rules.why: SAP Note 3255746 ('Unpermitted usage of ODP Data Replication APIs') triggered an 'are we affected?' question. The failure mode is reasoning from the category: assuming any data-extraction RFC is in scope. ODP is a replication framework (delta queues, subscriptions, change-data-capture); RFC_READ_TABLE is a generic single-table SELECT-equivalent with no delta queue and no subscription. Conflating them produces either a false 'we are non-compliant' panic or -- worse -- a false 'we are safe' on a note that DID hit us. Precision on the exact API IS the whole answer (CP-003: precision + evidence + facts).
rules.how_to_apply:
1) Grep the repo for the SPECIFIC restricted FMs/namespaces named in the note (e.g. RODPS_REPL, ODQ_, /SAPDS/) -- report the call count with file:line.
2) Identify the FM our pipeline actually calls (read rfc_helpers.py / extract_*.py) and cite it.
3) Produce a restricted-vs-used comparison so the verdict is auditable.
4) Recommend running SAP's own self-assessment tool (when the note ships one, e.g. Note 3439624) to convert code evidence into SAP-sourced confirmation.
5) If the pipeline depends on a single non-released FM (RFC_READ_TABLE), flag it as a forward-looking risk and name the SAP-endorsed durable path (ODP-OData / Business Data Cloud).

rules.rule: No research/analysis produces conclusions or plans until it is CLOSED. A research is CLOSED only when ALL 8 guarantees pass: (1) completeness, (2) graded sources, (3) adversarial verification finished, (4) citable evidence per claim, (5) explicit confidence tier, (6) gaps stated as open questions, (7) reproducibility, (8) no-spin attestation. An incomplete/stopped/failed run is OPEN -> discard or re-run; NEVER salvage its fragments into findings. Conclusions and plans are built ONLY on CLOSED claims, each carrying its tier + citation; anything on a LOW/open item is labeled ASSUMPTION/RISK.
